notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on: whether the 1839 stone tower existed (Friends omit it), the 1858 work (rebuild or renovation), land price ($140 vs $160), Emerson rescue date (16 vs 17 March 1865), British vs Canadian award, murder date (1 June per 1896 papers and Lighthousefriends; 2 June per D'Entremont), and lantern removal (late 1960s vs 1972). The 1865 article is OCR; vessel spelled Edith Ann. No Light-House Board report from the 1850s was in the corpus (lhb begins 1891), so the 1858 and 1854 claims rest on secondary accounts. Reidy and 1952-era Coast Guard names left out of the roster except as USLHS prints. D'Entremont's page includes recollections of a relief keeper from the 1960s, not used by name.
